evals.prompt: Review Dependabot PR #890 in schemalabz/opencouncil as it stood at head e2c9f7923 on base 009e4fb3c, and give me a verdict on whether we should merge it. I want to be confident nothing breaks.
evals.run_constraints: The PR is merged now: treat it as open at the pinned head. Post nothing. No next build, no dev server, no full test suites in either arm (same constraint for both, so the comparison is about analysis). npm ci, tsc, npm diff, reading CI logs and read-only doctl are allowed.

ground_truth.direct_changes: 45 root dependencies change in package-lock.json, plus direct dependencies of workspace packages: @google/genai 2.27.0->2.30.0 (packages/subject-images) and libphonenumber-js 1.13.14->1.13.15 (packages/ui). An inventory that reads only the root package.json misses these two (the orchestrator did, 2026-10-20).
ground_truth.nix_failure: @posthog/nextjs-config 1.11.1->1.11.3 moves @posthog/cli to ~0.18.10; @posthog/webpack-plugin 1.7.1 pins ~0.16.2, so npm nests a second cli copy; flake.nix mkNpmDeps patches only the top-level copy; the nested postinstall reaches github.com in the sandbox (EAI_AGAIN).
ground_truth.tsc_failure: TS2741 at src/lib/ai.ts:318: @anthropic-ai/sdk 0.135 adds required Usage.speed.
ground_truth.deploy_time_change: nextjs-config 1.11.3 adds a Turbopack native-debug-ID path: posthog-cli release resolve at config load (a non-zero exit fails the build), sourcemap upload instead of process, deletion of all .map files. Both deployed environments run the source-map step at build time, so both run the new path.
ground_truth.environments: Staging lacks the cache integration that production has (visible in the deployment spec and the staging run log), so nextjs-cache-handler 3.4 is first exercised for real in production. Bot PRs get no preview (the preview job skips bot authors).
ground_truth.untested_surfaces: No test executes: AWS SDK S3 paths (s3.ts, presigned-url route, set-acl), nextjs-cache-handler, react-email rendering (mocked), marked, react-easy-crop, posthog-node/@posthog/mcp, most Radix primitives (1 rendering test file). mcp-handler had no test before the review.
ground_truth.gain: next 16.4.x security fixes (GHSA-p3m5-59mp-jv5r, GHSA-2464-fhr4-w9xw); nextjs-cache-handler 3.4 seeds the keys Next >=16.3.8 reads.
ground_truth.verified_by: 2026-10-20: CI logs, local tsc, a local production build, a manual surface pass over every untested package, and the staging and production deploy logs after the merge.

process: Builds the list of changed packages from the lockfile diff (or npm ls on both sides), and states its size; does not rely on the PR title or body for it
Gives every changed runtime or build-time package (or a named group of them) its own evidence level, so an untested package is visible as a row, not folded into one free-text line
Reads the package's own diff (npm diff or the installed dist) for at least one build/deploy-time package, and names what changes at deploy time
For each item without evidence, names the environment that can produce it (local test, local build, preview, staging after merge, production only)
Derives staging-versus-production differences from the deployment spec or logs rather than assuming staging mirrors production
Includes a list of tests the repo should have for these dependencies, separate from the merge verdict
correctness: Attributes the Nix Checks failure to the nested @posthog/cli copy, not to 'the group'
Attributes the tsc error to the @anthropic-ai/sdk Usage type change
Claims no package change that is not in the lockfile diff (note: @google/genai and libphonenumber-js ARE in it, through workspace packages)
Does not claim that staging exercises the Valkey cache
tie: Names the Next 16.4 security fixes as the main gain
Verdict is needs-work (or equivalent) with the two concrete fixes

evals.notes: Assertions written 2026-10-25 before the candidate skill and before any run. evals.prompt: Review Dependabot PR #938 in schemalabz/opencouncil as it stood at head 71a789aa0fec9aea8752b46153998105c1fff769, with fdb60324ba0e4013cca93868e36e2d1d974e3542 as main, and give me a verdict on whether we should merge it.
evals.run_constraints: The PR is merged now: treat it as open at the pinned head and treat the pinned base as main; do not read commits after the base. Post nothing, push nothing. nix builds, npm ci, tsc, jest of single folders and npm diff are allowed; no next build.

ground_truth.payload: yargs 17.7.2 -> 18.2.0 (root and packages/seed-pipeline); @types/yargs stays (yargs 18 types only ./browser).
ground_truth.ci: Nix Checks, Integration and Notis green on the PR head.
ground_truth.failure: Both Nix seed bundles (seed-pipeline-bundle, seed-bundle) BUILD but crash at load: esbuild --format=cjs replaces import.meta with {}, so createRequire(import.meta.url) in yargs 18 / yargs-parser 22 throws ERR_INVALID_ARG_VALUE. The flake checks build the bundles but never run them. Previews run the seed bundle at database init, so every migration-PR preview would fail.
ground_truth.fix: define import.meta.url as the bundle file URL in both esbuild calls + an install check that runs each bundle with --help (54756cdb5, merged as part of #938 on 2026-11-07).
ground_truth.landing: The fix exists only because of the bump and needs no preview -> push onto the Dependabot branch (what was done).
ground_truth.verified_by: 2026-11-07 review (938.md) + orchestrator build of both bundles on the fixed head, and CI installCheckPhase after the merge.

process: Lists the Nix seed bundles (or 'the esbuild bundles') as build targets that load yargs, separately from Jest/tsx
Runs at least one built bundle (for example its --help) on the PR head, not only builds it, and reports what happened
Reviews the pinned head (rebased locally if needed) without asking Dependabot to rebase and without posting
The verdict states the exact payload versions
Names where a fix would land (onto the Dependabot branch or a separate PR) and why
correctness: Reports that the bundles crash at load on the PR head, with the import.meta/createRequire cause
States that CI being green does not cover the bundles' runtime
tie: Overall clarity and completeness of the report (inventory, verdict, evidence)
